title: Meeting Erroll Garner at the Casablanca and learning how to play with him
summary: Garner sat in at the San Pedro club; from Garner's left Callender saw that his strong left hand set the beat.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Erroll Garner and I first met... I don't know whether I mentioned this before, but I had a group, a trio, and I think it was a little joint on San Pedro, near Adams, called the Casablanca. I had the trio. My piano player was Jack LaRue and my guitarist was Leonard Enois, whose nickname was Lucky Enois. All these guys are gone, incidentally. But Erroll Garner came in one night, and asked to sit in, and I had never experienced anything like it. Fortunately, I was on his left; I played on his left side. So I spied how to play with him. Because most of the guys who worked with Erroll listened to his right hand, which always seemed to be lagging. Which it really wasn't. He carried such a strong beat in his left hand until it
was... Right away I said, "Hey, I know how to play with this guy."
